items.q: An infant has weeping cheeks sparing the nose tip, later shifting to flexural lichenified patches. This march fits?
items.exp: Atopic dermatitis starts on infant cheeks then moves to flexures with dry lichenified itchy plaques.
r: Correct. Cheeks then flexures with lichenification.
Incorrect. That is greasy yellow in folds.
Incorrect. That favours extensors with silvery scale.
Incorrect. That burrows webs with nocturnal itch.
items.kp: Cheeks to flexures march is atopic dermatitis.

items.q: Extra eyelid crease, periorbital darkening and white dermographism in an itchy flexural rash point to?
items.exp: Dennie-Morgan folds, allergic shiners and white dermographism are minor signs of the atopic constitution.
r: Incorrect. That needs exposure history with patch tests.
Incorrect. That shows hyphae on KOH.
Incorrect. That is photosensitive with systemic features.
Correct. Atopic minor signs cluster.
items.kp: Dennie-Morgan plus white dermographism is atopy.

items.q: Greasy yellow scales on the scalp margins, eyebrows and nasolabial folds with dandruff suggest?
items.exp: Seborrhoeic dermatitis targets sebaceous areas with greasy yellow scale linked to Malassezia.
r: Incorrect. That gives dry silvery thick plaques.
Incorrect. That breaks hairs with dots.
Correct. Greasy yellow sebaceous-area scale.
Incorrect. That is dry flexural lichenification.
items.kp: Greasy yellow folds scale is seborrhoeic dermatitis.

items.q: A construction worker has dry fissured dorsal-hand eczema sparing the palms, worse after cement contact. The mechanism is?
o: Irritant contact dermatitis with barrier disruption
items.exp: Cement alkalis strip barrier lipids causing dorsal irritant eczema; allergy would need patch-test proof and often involves palms.
r: Incorrect. That gives well-defined plaques.
Correct. Alkaline irritant dorsal hand disease.
Incorrect. Type I gives urticaria, not chronic fissures.
Incorrect. KOH would show hyphae.
items.kp: Cement dorsal-hand fissures mean irritant dermatitis.

items.q: Nickel earlobe rash with itchy vesicles 48 hours after wearing earrings is mediated by?
items.exp: Allergic contact dermatitis is T-cell delayed hypersensitivity confirmed by patch testing.
r: Correct. Delayed T-cell reaction.
Incorrect. IgE gives immediate wheal.
Incorrect. Cytotoxicity lyses blood cells.
Incorrect. Complexes give vasculitis.

items.q: Coin-shaped exudative intensely itchy plaques on the limbs in winter suggest?
items.exp: Discoid eczema gives round weeping coin lesions in dry winter skin, often with Staph colonisation.
r: Incorrect. That has active advancing edges.
Incorrect. That has extensor silvery plaques.
Incorrect. That has violaceous polygons.
Correct. Coin-shaped winter exudation.
items.kp: Winter coin exudation is nummular eczema.

items.q: Brown staining above the ankles with itchy scaly patches, woody induration and healed ulcers indicates?
items.exp: Venous hypertension leaks haemosiderin and fibrin, giving gaiter eczema, inverted-champagne induration and ulcer risk.
r: Incorrect. That gives yellow atrophic plaques.
Incorrect. That gives non-pitting thyroid shins.
Correct. Gaiter staining with woody induration.
Incorrect. That is hot spreading with fever.
items.kp: Gaiter staining with woodiness is venous eczema.

items.q: Deep tapioca-like vesicles on the palms with burning itch in summer is?
items.exp: Pompholyx gives deep-seated sago vesicles on palms and soles with intense itch in warm months.
r: Incorrect. That adds mouth ulcers.
Correct. Sago-grain palmar vesicles.
Incorrect. That gives thick plaques with fissures.
Incorrect. That burrows finger webs.

items.q: The baseline of all eczema care regardless of type is?
o: Regular emollients with trigger avoidance and gentle skin care
items.exp: Barrier repair with emollients, soap substitutes and trigger control underpins every eczema plan before active topicals.
r: Correct. Moisturise, protect and avoid triggers.
Incorrect. Systemic steroids are rescue only.
Incorrect. Antibiotics only cover infection.
Incorrect. Lukewarm short baths are allowed.
items.kp: Every eczema plan starts with emollients.

items.q: Weeping golden-crust superinfection over eczema with sudden flare needs?
items.exp: Infected eczema with crusting and flare signals Staph superinfection needing antimicrobial cover with ongoing barrier care.
r: Incorrect. Steroids alone feed infection.
Incorrect. Fungi are not the driver.
Incorrect. Itch control alone misses infection.
Correct. Cover the superinfection too.
items.kp: Crusted flare means add antistaphylococcal cover.
